entries.title: Curriculum
entries.short: A structured learning plan that ties goals, content, methods and assessment together.
entries.long:
## What is a curriculum?

In education, a curriculum (plural: curricula) is a
structured plan and systematic concept for how learning
and teaching happen.

## Four core questions

Every curriculum answers four central questions:

- **Learning goals (why?)** — Which competencies should be
  acquired?
- **Learning content (what?)** — Which topics will be
  covered?
- **Methodology and didactics (how?)** — Which teaching and
  learning forms will be used?
- **Evaluation (how well?)** — How will learning success be
  measured?

## Difference from a syllabus

A curriculum puts the learner and their competency acquisition
at the center (outcome orientation), not just a rigid list of
subject areas. A syllabus documents **what** should be taught;
a curriculum also describes **why** and **how** — and measures
**what was actually learned**.

## Four dimensions

Curriculum research distinguishes four manifestations:

- **Intended curriculum** — the documented target.
- **Implemented curriculum** — what is actually taught.
- **Achieved curriculum** — what learners actually
  understand.
- **Hidden curriculum** — implicit learning that happens
  alongside (study habits, attitudes, social norms).

## In Adaptive Learner

In Adaptive Learner, a curriculum is your personal learning
plan for a topic. It organizes learning topics hierarchically
and ties them to lessons. You define the goals, content and
methods — the system supports the evaluation through
tracking, the learning profile and AI feedback after each
step.

Unlike a printed curriculum, this one adapts continuously:
when a method-switch recommendation appears, it is the
implemented curriculum reacting to the achieved one.

entries.title: Learning Project
entries.short: Your concrete learning effort with topic, goal, timeframe and daily learning time.
entries.long:
## What is a learning project?

A learning project bundles everything that belongs to a
learning effort: the topic, your goal, the timeframe, and
your daily learning time. It is the bracket around your
sessions, your curriculum and your learning profile.

## Why these four fields?

- **Topic** — what you want to learn (e.g., "Spanish for
  travel", "Python basics", "C major piano scale").
  Concrete and bounded, not too broad.
- **Goal** — what you want to be able to do at the end.
  Concrete goals ("order food at a restaurant") produce
  better AI prompts than vague ones ("learn Spanish").
- **Timeframe** — by when. Affects how aggressively the
  system schedules repetitions and when the method-switch
  recommendation appears.
- **Daily learning time** — how many minutes per day you
  can invest. Drives the spaced-repetition recommendations
  and session length.

## Why concrete goals matter

Learning research is clear: SMART goals (specific,
measurable, attractive, realistic, time-bound) double
learning success compared to vague intentions. Adaptive
Learner translates your goal into the AI's system prompt;
the more concrete you are, the sharper the generated
exercises.

## In Adaptive Learner

You can have several learning projects in parallel. Each
session belongs to exactly one project; your progress
(XP, badges, streak) is tracked per project. When you
change the timeframe, the system automatically adjusts the
repetition cadence — a tight timeframe staggers
repetitions more densely.

entries.title: Learning Profile
entries.short: Your personal strength profile across six learning methods, derived from the assessment test.
entries.long:
## What is the learning profile?

The learning profile shows how well each of the six
Adaptive Learner methods suits you. It comes from your
answers in the assessment test (12 questions) and is
visualized as a radar chart.

## The six axes

Each axis is a method with a weight between 0 and 100:

- **Deductive** — learn the rule, then apply it.
- **Inductive** — see examples, derive the rule yourself.
- **Error-based** — make mistakes deliberately, then
  understand why.
- **Dialogic** — learn through conversation.
- **Contextual** — learn in simulated everyday situations.
- **AI-adaptive** — the system picks automatically.

## It is a profile, not a label

Nobody is "a deductive learner". Every learner has a
weighted pattern across all six methods. A profile with
high inductive and dialogic weights does not mean
deductive will not work for you — it means the other two
typically get you to learning success faster.

## Changes over time

The learning profile is not carved in stone. With every
completed learning cycle and every method switch, the
system adjusts its recommendations. You can re-take the
assessment test at any time — typically useful every
3-6 months, or after a major topic change.

## In Adaptive Learner

The profile drives the dashboard view and session
recommendations. If you start a session without specifying
a method, the system picks the method with the highest
weight in your profile.

entries.title: Learning Session
entries.short: An AI-driven learning unit that follows the 7-step cycle.
entries.long:
## What is a learning session?

A learning session is a continuous learning unit on one
topic, driven by the 7-step cycle (input, attempt, error,
feedback, adapt, repeat, integrate). The AI plays the
teacher role; you drive the dialog.

## What makes a session different from a chat?

In a session the **dual-prompt evaluator** runs alongside:
after every answer, a second AI instance judges your
understanding (0-100% confidence) and decides whether you
are ready for the next step. A regular chat has no such
corrective.

## Streaming

The AI's answers appear word by word (Server-Sent Events)
so you do not wait for the full reply. You can interrupt
at any time and ask follow-ups — the session runs until
you end it or the cycle completes.

## When should I end a session?

- After step 7 (integrate), when the learning cycle is
  complete.
- When the system recommends a method switch and you
  accept the recommendation.
- When your **stress** rating has been above 4 in the
  last few ratings — a break is more productive than
  pushing through.

## Ratings carry forward

Every session ends with three sliders (understanding,
stress, method fit, each 1-5). These values feed into
your learning profile and shape future recommendations:
sustained high stress plus low method fit triggers the
method-switch recommendation.

## In Adaptive Learner

A session belongs to exactly one learning project. You
can have only one active session at a time; this prevents
topic mixing and shields the method-switch logic from
noise.
